added_failures_note: measured by running the same focused selection at the reviewed base and head in scratch trees: tests/discovery/test_reset.py at 4ac20c26 gives 31 passed EXIT=0, at 21faa85ad gives 1 failed/30 passed EXIT=1; the single added failure is the pre-existing target-list test, which the reviewed run also recorded in its own precommit-tests.log

findings.text: adding the retry-failed key to CODE_RESET_SPECS changes get_valid_targets("code"), so the pre-existing test that asserts the fixed target list now fails; the reviewed head reproduces it (1 failed/30 passed) while the base passes (31 passed), and both the reviewed run's precommit-tests.log and the manifest follow_ons name it. The file is outside the node's declared write scope and sibling run r-20261008T132726299004-reset-target-list-test is repairing it, so this is an added failure the node correctly reported rather than fixed.

the two-worker code pass logged 62 ingested events (10+10+10+10+10+10+2) for 46 unique target paths after duplicate same-batch claims, which the graph check then collapses to 46 unique ingested paths; the duplicate work is redundant LLM/embedding spend and risks double CodeChunks, and the node declares it as a follow-on rather than owning the claiming fix.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the target is consumed at imas_codex/cli/discover/code.py:148 via CODE_RESET_SPECS[reset_to] and surfaced through click.Choice(get_valid_targets("code")) in imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py, so --reset-to retry-failed reaches the spec without further wiring.
item_verdicts.diff: two commits against 4ac20c26 add a 6-line retry-failed ResetSpec (target scored, source failed only, clearing ingested_at/error/skip_reason) and one 44-line test; no other product code changes.
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan comment's done-when is met: a test shows failed moved and ingested untouched, and all 46 JT-60SA files were reset to scored and re-ingested with errors cleared, verified against the graph.
item_verdicts.goal: the node adds a code reset target taking only failed files back to scored through the shared reset specs, exposed as --reset-to retry-failed, and reprocesses the 46 /home CodeFiles left at failed by a transient SSH drop.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records two commits (054fc64f4, 21faa85ad), the focused/operational/graph logs, a mutation negative control, and empty baseline_suite/after_suite.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff touches exactly two of the declared paths, imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py and tests/discovery/test_code_retry_failed_reset.py, and nothing else; the evidence-fragment path declared in orientation is not produced by these commits.

justifications.durability: the new target is guarded by a test that fails under a declared mutation (adding ingested to the source statuses makes the count 2 instead of 1), so the failed-only behaviour cannot silently regress inside this node; the repository suite is nonetheless left red because the added key breaks an out-of-scope test that the node cannot touch.
justifications.evidence: baseline/after focused logs, the operational reset and ingest receipts, and a graph check that proves 46 unique targets ingested with empty errors all trace the claim, but the pre-registered baseline test asserting get_valid_targets was dropped in 21faa85ad so the base and after arms do not run the same test, and the initial 5,002-ingested figure is asserted in evidence_inputs without a log behind it.
justifications.fit: the spec key follows the existing CODE_RESET_SPECS vocabulary, the commits carry conventional subjects with bodies, the test is named by mechanism, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in the code or messages.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the target, the CLI exposure, the failed-only filter and the 46-file reprocess are all present and verified; the only unfulfilled clause is the plan's optional error-text filter, omitted legitimately since the plan marks it optional.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses reset_to_status and the shared ResetSpec mechanism rather than adding a bespoke path, and the new spec restates the field set of the neighbouring scored spec as every spec in the block does.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff stays inside the declared write scope; the one broken test and the duplicate-claim behaviour are both outside it and are reported as follow-ons rather than edited.
